paper_id: Yang et al. - 2013 - Detecting Outlier Measurements Based on Graph Rigidity for Wireless Sensor Network Localization
title: Detecting Outlier Measurements Based on Graph Rigidity for Wireless Sensor Network Localization
motivation: Outlier ranging measurements severely degrade localization accuracy, yet existing triangle inequality methods fail to precisely identify outliers
problem_framing: Given a distance graph G, determine if an edge e=(u,v) is an outlier by checking if G-e still contains enough information to compute distance(u,v)
key_insight: If G-e is globally rigid, the distance between u and v is uniquely determined across all realizations, allowing definitive verification of W(e)
method_signature: Verifiable edge detection via globally rigid subgraphs and MGRS voting for outlier sifting
evaluation_criteria: Percentage of verifiable edges/graphs vs node density; location error with/without outlier sifting
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Sufficient and necessary conditions for edge verifiability remain an open problem; MGRS finding lacks theoretical foundation
thinking_moves: 把定位问题中'足够信息'反推为图论中全局刚性的冗余约束
从单边验证扩展到整图验证,建立层级化的理论条件
承认充分必要条件未知,主动限定研究范围排除棘手情况
引入MGRS概念将验证问题转化为最小支撑子图搜索问题
cites_own_work: Z. Yang et al. 2010 - Beyond trilateration
T. Eren et al. 2004 - Rigidity computation randomization
